sofi_happy_path.description: SoFi Relay export — clean headers close to Budgy schema, expense-negative amounts. Should be the highest-scoring fixture.

plan.column_map_reasoning: All columns map cleanly to Budgy schema fields. The CSV headers are explicit and match the schema exactly. 'Authorized Date', 'Posted Date', and 'Status' are standard fields. 'Account Name' identifies the account. 'Description' contains transaction details. 'Primary Category' and 'Detailed Category' are the category fields. 'Amount' is the transaction amount.
plan.category_map_reasoning: All category values map to valid Budgy primary and detailed category pairs. Merchant names (e.g., 'Starbucks', 'Target', 'Netflix') are mapped to their transaction type: Starbucks → Coffee shops, Target/Amazon → Retail, Netflix/Spotify → Entertainment. Generic categories like 'Pharmacy', 'Fitness', 'Rent' map directly. Payroll and transfer terms ('Direct Deposit Payroll', 'Venmo Transfer', 'Person to person payments') map to Income and Transfers. Categories that appear to be already-hierarchical in the raw data (e.g., 'Housing & utilities', 'Shopping', 'Transportation', 'Entertainment', 'Food & drink', 'Health & wellness', 'Income') are treated as primary categories and map to themselves with a reasonable detailed subcategory based on context. A few values ('Transfers', 'Primary Category', 'Detailed Category', 'Housing & utilities', 'Shopping', 'Transportation', 'Entertainment', 'Food & drink', 'Health & wellness', 'Income') appear to be already-mapped primary categories and are mapped to themselves as primary with 'Other' subtype where context is ambiguous.
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: The sample amounts show one positive value (3200.0, likely an income transaction from wages/payroll) and nine negative values (ranging from -6.75 to -110.0, all expenses). This follows the standard 'expense_negative' convention where expenses are negative numbers and income is positive. No transformation is needed on import.

chase.description: Chase checking export — no category column (all rows will soft-fail to 'Other'/Unchecked), has 'Balance' and 'Check or Slip #' columns that must be dropped, expense-negative amounts.

'Amount' is the transaction amount. 'Type' appears to contain category-like values and maps to primary_category (though the actual values are merchant names rather than categories—see category_map section). 'Balance' is account balance, not transaction-level data, so it's excluded. 'Check or Slip #' is a reference identifier, mapped to notes for context. 'Details' is redundant with Description and Balance combined, so it's unmapped.

I've mapped each merchant to its most appropriate Budgy primary+detailed category pair based on the business type: fitness centers to Health & wellness, ride-sharing to Transportation, retail stores to Shopping, gas stations to Transportation, pharmacies to Shopping, Amazon to Shopping, Venmo to person-to-person transfers, rent to Housing & utilities, coffee shops to Food & drink, streaming services to Entertainment, salary deposits to Income, utilities to Housing & utilities, restaurants to Food & drink, and grocery stores to Food & drink. CVS was mapped to Shopping (Retail) rather than Pharmacy because the CSV does not distinguish pharmacy purchases from general retail.
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: All Amount values in the sample are either negative (e.g., -87.43, -6.75, -42.5, -15.99, -58.2, -45.0, -110.0, -23.18, -18.5) or positive (3200.0). The single positive value (3200.0) matches the pattern of a direct deposit payroll (DIRECT DEP PAYROLL ADP), which is income. All other transactions are negative, consistent with expenses. This follows the standard 'expense_negative' convention where expenses are negative numbers and income is positive.

apple_card.description: Apple Card export — expense-positive amounts (expenses are positive numbers, Type=Debit), both Description and Merchant columns present (AI should prefer Merchant as description), has 'Purchased By' to drop.

Clearing Date maps to posted_date as it represents when the transaction cleared the account. Description and Merchant both contain transaction details; Description is the primary field, Merchant goes to notes for additional context. Category maps to primary_category as the raw values will be transformed to valid Budgy categories. Type appears to be a transaction type indicator (income vs expense) rather than a category, so it's mapped to null since Budgy infers direction from amount sign. Amount (USD) clearly maps to amount. Purchased By likely indicates the cardholder or account holder, mapping to account_name.

Merchant names like Starbucks, Shell, CVS, etc. are mapped to their most specific category (e.g., Starbucks → Coffee shops, Shell/Gas → Gas & EV charging). Broader categories like "Health," "Housing," "Shopping," "Transportation," and "Entertainment" are mapped to their category families with "Other" detailed subcategories. "Payroll Direct Deposit" clearly indicates income wages. "Payments" is interpreted as generic transfers. Grocery retailers (Whole Foods, Chipotle) are mapped to appropriate food categories.
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: The sample Amount (USD) values are all positive numbers (3200.0, 87.43, 6.75, 42.5, 15.99, 58.2, 45.0, 110.0, 23.18, 18.5). Without negative examples in the sample, I inferred the sign convention by examining the category mix: the presence of "Payroll Direct Deposit" (income) alongside expense categories like "Pharmacy," "Rent," and "Gas Station" suggests mixed transaction types. In standard banking conventions, the 'expense_negative' format is most common. However, since all sample values are positive, there is some ambiguity. Given that this appears to be a real bank export with both income and expenses, I've assumed the standard convention where expenses are negative and income is positive, with the caveat that the actual sign convention should be verified by checking a few rows from the original CSV where the Type column clearly indicates whether each transaction is income or expense.

Income transactions (Paycheck, DIRECT DEP PAYROLL ADP, Payroll) map to Income > Wages. Rent-related entries (Rent, January rent, LANDLORD RENT PMT) map to Housing & utilities > Rent. Utilities map to Housing & utilities > Gas & electricity. Groceries and grocery stores (Whole Foods, weekly shop) map to Food & drink > Groceries. Coffee shops (Starbucks, morning coffee) map to Food & drink > Coffee shops. Restaurants (Chipotle, lunch, split dinner) map to Food & drink > Restaurants & bars. Retail purchases (Target, Amazon, household items, Shopping) map to Shopping > Retail. Gas stations (Shell, Gas & Fuel) map to Transportation > Gas & EV charging. Rideshare (Uber) maps to Transportation > Taxi & ride shares. Fitness (Planet Fitness, Health & Fitness) maps to Health & wellness > Fitness. Pharmacy/CVS maps to Health & wellness > Pharmacy. Entertainment subscriptions (Netflix, Spotify, streaming) map to their respective Entertainment subcategories. Transfers (Transfer, Venmo, VENMO PAYMENT) map to Transfers > Account transfers or Person to person payments. Home is mapped broadly to Housing & utilities > Other housing & utilities.

Given the ambiguity and that income values ($2,800, $500) are clearly income while typical expenses are mixed in, I'm inferring 'expense_negative' as the most likely intended convention — meaning expenses should be imported as negative on normalization. If this is incorrect, the user should clarify whether expenses or income should be negated.
